newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pick AGM rejects equity hike, approves div.
newsitem.headline: Pick AGM rejects equity hike, approves div.

text.p: Shareholders of Hungarian meat processor Pick Szeged Rt rejected a plan on Monday to authorise the board to increase equity capital by up to 20 percent to pay for new acquisitions.
The board failed to win approval for the proposal from the necessary two-thirds majority at the company's annual shareholders meeting, with just over 50 percent voting in favour.

Shareholders did approve the board's previous recommendation of a 200 forints per share dividend on the 1996 earnings and also approved the plan by the company to expand into the mineral water business.

Pick announced that it expected to improve its pre-tax profits to 2.8 billion forints in 1997 after announcing earlier a consolidated pre-tax profits of 2.48 billion forints in 1996 on net sales of 28.56 billion.

General Director Vilmos Bihari told Reuters he was not too disappointed that shareholders rejected the equity capital increase proposal because the directors had not presented any specific acquisitions plans.

"The increase is big and they (the shareholders) want to know what the company is going to buy," he said, adding that the board had hoped by the proposal to avoid having to hold another general meeting to approve any large acquisitions.
He said Pick had some acquisitions in Hungary in mind, but he said he was not authorised to provide any details.
Pick's last major acquisition was for rival Herz.
Bihari said the company's 1997 pre-tax profit forecast was "an underestimation, a very careful estimation".
"There are lots of topics to discuss, a lot of resolutions and the future depends on these resolutions," he said.
"If we want to buy anything and we can only get the increase in capital somewhat later on then the credit that we will have to use in the meantime will of course worsen the figure," he said.
Bihari also said Pick expected exports to increase to $75 million from $72 million even though its main export market in Germany had been hurt by the German economic downturn.
"In CEFTA we will have some possibilities for growth," he said, noting that sales in Poland had increased 75 percent.
